validity.recommendation: Merge P7864 ("Nitzana Pipeline") into P3620 — same physical pipe; keep one row, carry P7864's diameter (36 in) onto P3620.
validity.researcher_notes: P3620 is REAL and correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk — no existence or classification doubt. The dispositive finding is a DUPLICATE against roster row P7864 "Nitzana Pipeline" (65 km, dia 36, cap 600, proposed). Independent sources make clear these are ONE project, which the industry literally calls the "Nitzana pipeline": Chevron/NewMed/Ratio + state operator Israel Natural Gas Lines (INGL) signed a $610M EPC in Sept 2025 for a 36-inch, ~65–67 km line from Ramat Hovav (Negev) to the Nitzana crossing on the Egypt border, moving 600 MMcf/d (≈ 6 bcm/y) of Leviathan gas, plus a new compressor station at Ramat Hovav, targeting 2028 operation. That matches P3620's endpoints (Ramat Hovav→Nitzana), length (65 km), and capacity (6 bcm/y = 600 MMcf/d) exactly, and matches P7864's name, length (65), diameter (36) and capacity (600). P7864 is a relabel/re-discovery of the same pipe (added 2025-12-23, after P3620) and should be merged. NOTE: P3657 "Israel–Egypt Offshore Gas Pipeline" (offshore, cap 6.7) is a distinct older proposal — NOT a duplicate of P3620; keep separate. Sources: Times of Israel (timesofisrael, 2025-09), Offshore Technology (2025-09-18), JNS (2023-07-02), MEES (2025-09-19).

validity.recommendation: Update SegmentCost — the recorded $200M is a stale 2021 estimate; the awarded EPC is $610M (2023 cabinet-approved project value was ~$246M / 900M shekels).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost = $200,000,000, which traces to a 2021-vintage Offshore Technology figure. Current independent reporting contradicts it: the May-2023 Israeli cabinet approval put the project at 900M shekels (~$246M) [JNS], and the Sept-2025 EPC contract signed with INGL is a $610M project value [Times of Israel; Offshore Technology; ENR]. The $200M figure is materially wrong/outdated. I did NOT stage a $200M ref (no source supports it). Human choice needed on which basis to record (project capex vs the 15-yr EPC value); leaving SegmentCost unresolved rather than overwriting.

fills.researcher_notes: 65 km stated by JNS (2023, "65 kilometers... Ramat Hovav to Nitzana") and Offshore Technology (2025, "65-km"). Some trade outlets say 67 km (constructionreviewonline) — 65 is well within reporting range.
State-owned Israel Natural Gas Lines (INGL) is the builder/owner-operator under the $610M EPC. Confirmed by Offshore Technology and Times of Israel.
Route Ramat Hovav (southern Israel/Negev) to the Nitzana crossing on the Israel–Egypt border (JNS notes it passes through Ashalim). Confirmed by JNS and Offshore Technology.

Existing Capacity ref (energy-sea.gov.il, Israeli Ministry of Energy announcement, May 2023) DOES support the value — it states the line 'is projected to allow for an additional 6 BCM of natural gas to be exported to Egypt annually', i.e. 6 bcm/y; keep the existing ref. (An earlier note wrongly called it unconfirmable — the prose 'annually' phrasing was missed by a substring check.) Independent corroboration: JNS states "6 billion cubic meters annually"; Offshore Technology states "at least 600 million cubic feet per day" (≈ 6.2 bcm/y). 6 bcm/y confirmed.

Diameter blank in GEM P3620. Trade reporting on the Sept-2025 project describes "a 36-in., 67-km pipeline and a new compressor station at Ramat Hovav." Also matches duplicate row P7864 (dia 36). Tier medium: figure is echoed across outlets that largely trace to the Sept-2025 Chevron/INGL announcement (limited origin independence).

The Israeli Cabinet approved the ~900M-shekel export-pipeline project in May 2023. Primary support: the Ministry of Energy's own announcement (energy-sea.gov.il, already the row's Capacity ref) — its May-2023 dateline itself supports ProposalYear 2023 (and ProposalMonth=5 if the reviewer wants it). Plus JNS coverage; MEES 2023-05-12 and Enerdata independently corroborate (see the Proposal ref_work unit). Official primary record of the approval event + independent trade coverage → high. (Concept was first floated Oct 2021; 2023 is the formal government-approval year.)

Recorded $200M is a stale 2021 estimate contradicted by newer sources ($246M project cost in 2023; $610M EPC in 2025). No independent source supports $200M, so no ref staged (standing rule 2). Flagged as a spec concern for human update; left unresolved.

DelayType='inferred' has no source and none was found. The project actually advanced on schedule (EPC Sept 2025, govt approval Dec 2025, Leviathan expansion FID Jan 2026), so the inferred-delay flag looks unsupported; recommend clearing. No ref staged.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'construction' confirmed. Timeline of dated evidence: $610M EPC signed with INGL Sept 2025 with construction slated to start Q4 2025 and ~3-yr build to 2028 operation [Offshore Technology, Times of Israel]; Israeli govt gave final approval to the $35bn Leviathan–Egypt export deal underpinning the line in Dec 2025; Leviathan expansion FID ($2.36bn), which feeds this export route, was taken Jan 2026 [Rigzone]. CAVEAT: I did not find an independent report explicitly stating pipe-laying/groundbreaking has physically begun — 'construction' rests on the awarded EPC + FID + approvals + scheduled Q4-2025 start, which is a reasonable basis. Most recent evidence 2026-01. Not operating, not shelved — no downgrade warranted.

summary: P3620 is real (gas transmission, Ramat Hovav→Nitzana, 65km/36in/6bcm-y, INGL, Leviathan) but is a DUPLICATE of P7864 'Nitzana Pipeline'; SegmentCost $200M is a stale spec (now $610M EPC); status 'construction' confirmed (EPC Sept-2025 + FID Jan-2026).
